countries.page_length_note: One to two pages. Two is normal even for a first job here — a strict one-page limit is a United States convention, not a local one.
countries.photo_note: A passport-style photo is conventional on a Cambodian CV. Plain background, recent, business dress.
include_personal_details: city or province you live in
Khmer and English proficiency, stated separately
omit_personal_details: salary expectations, unless the post asks for them
a referee's phone number before you have asked their permission
tone_notes: State Khmer and English levels explicitly. Most local posts ask for both, and leaving it out reads as a gap rather than an oversight.
Naming referees is normal practice here. Ask them before you list them.
University projects and coursework are expected content for a fresh graduate in this market, not padding.
Write in English unless the post itself is written in Khmer.
visa_terms: must be legally authorised to work in cambodia

countries.page_length_note: Two pages at most. One page is common and perfectly acceptable for a first job.
countries.photo_note: Leave the photo off. Singapore's fair-employment guidelines ask employers not to weigh age, gender, race, religion or marital status, and a photo puts several of those back on the page.
include_personal_details: the city you are currently based in
a one-line statement of your work-authorisation status
tone_notes: Open each bullet with what changed and close it with the number, if you have one.
Say plainly whether you need a work pass. Employers screen on it early, and being vague about it costs you the interview rather than delaying the question.
British spelling is standard.
Keep to a single column with ordinary headings. Multi-column and text-box layouts are read out of order by many resume parsers.

countries.page_length_note: Japan expects two documents rather than one: a 履歴書 (rirekisho) on the standard form, and a 職務経歴書 (shokumu keirekisho) describing what you actually did. Around two pages each.
countries.photo_note: The rirekisho has a photo box and it is expected to be filled: 3cm × 4cm, plain background, business dress, taken within the last three months.
omit_personal_details: self-promotion the evidence does not support
salary expectations, unless the post asks for them
unexplained gaps — every period should be accounted for
section_order: 免許・資格 Licences and certifications
志望動機 Reason for applying
tone_notes: List education and work history oldest first. A rirekisho is read forwards, which is the opposite of the reverse-chronological order every other market on this list expects.
Formal and factual. Understatement reads as competence here; overstatement reads as the absence of it.
Choose Gregorian years or Japanese era years and use that choice throughout. Mixing the two is the most common avoidable mistake.
The 志望動機 section is read closely. Write it for this employer specifically, not as a template.
visa_terms: 技術・人文知識・国際業務

countries.page_length_note: Two to three pages is normal and is not read as padding, which surprises people used to the one-page United States convention.
countries.photo_note: No photo. Australian employers screen against it for the same anti-discrimination reasons as Singapore.
include_personal_details: a one-line statement of your work rights
tone_notes: Plain English and no inflated titles. Overstating a role reads badly in this market.
'Referees available on request' is the conventional closing line. Have two people ready before you write it.
Government roles and many large employers ask you to answer selection criteria in a separate document. Check the posting before you apply.
State your work rights plainly — 'full working rights' is the phrase employers look for.

countries.page_length_note: One page for a first job. Two pages only once you have the paid experience to fill them.
countries.photo_note: No photo and no headshot in the header. United States employers screen against it on anti-discrimination grounds.
include_personal_details: city and country, or the word Remote
a one-line statement of your work-authorisation status
tone_notes: Open with a strong verb and close with a result. A number beats an adjective every time.
For a first job, Education can sit above Experience. Move it down once you have paid work to show.
Keep to a single column with ordinary headings. Multi-column and text-box layouts are read out of order by many resume parsers.
Check the time-zone overlap the post asks for before applying. A Phnom Penh working day overlaps a US Pacific one by very little.
Many roles advertised as United States remote require you to be living in the United States. That is a hard filter, not a preference.

us citizens and permanent residents only
must reside in the united states
eligible to work in the us
